gdp_level.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (DF_QNA, T0102) · Statistics Iceland's GDP at current prices, króna million, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Iceland produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to GDP in chain-linked volumes, also quarterly. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each year at its own ISK/USD rate (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual average), from 1981.

gdp_real.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (DF_QNA, T0102) · Statistics Iceland's GDP in chain-linked volumes, króna million, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current prices instead.
gdp_real.dollar: With “Make it real” on, “Dollarise” converts every period at one rate, the average for the latest year, so dollar growth equals real growth.

gdp_growth.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (DF_QNA, T0102) · Statistics Iceland's real GDP, seasonally adjusted, change on the previous quarter, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real terms, with regular seasonal patterns removed. Iceland's quarterly figures move a lot because the economy is small and lumpy.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying krónur to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

gdp_growth_yoy.source: OECD quarterly national accounts (DF_QNA, T0102) · Statistics Iceland's real GDP, seasonally adjusted, change on the same quarter a year earlier, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth_yoy.description: How much bigger or smaller the economy is than a year earlier, adjusted for inflation.
gdp_growth_yoy.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying krónur to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: OECD prices database · Statistics Iceland's national consumer price index, all items, monthly; change on the same month a year earlier, to one decimal place.
cpi.description: How much consumer prices have risen compared with a year earlier. This is Iceland's national index, which includes owner-occupied housing, not the EU's harmonised index. The Central Bank of Iceland targets 2.5%.

cpi_mom.source: OECD prices database · Statistics Iceland's national consumer price index, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, to one decimal place.
cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the latest month.

policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.IS, extended with the daily series D.IS) · the Central Bank of Iceland's key rate (seven-day term deposits), end of month, from June 2014; the current month shows the latest rate.
policy_rate.description: The key rate, the interest rate the Central Bank of Iceland sets to steer borrowing costs. The history starts in June 2014, when it took its current form; the BIS series runs back further using earlier, different rates, which are not shown.

unemployment.source: OECD infra-annual labour statistics (DF_IALFS_UNE_M) · Statistics Iceland's labour force survey, unemployment rate, 15 and over, seasonally adjusted, monthly.
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one.

exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports of goods, free on board, US$ converted to krónur at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly. Months where the IMF's import figure is a copy of its export figure are left out.
exports.description: The value of goods Iceland sells to the rest of the world each month, in krónur.
exports.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the krónur shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · imports of goods, cost, insurance and freight, US$ converted to krónur at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly. Months where the IMF's import figure is a copy of its export figure are left out.
imports.description: The value of goods Iceland buys from the rest of the world each month, in krónur.
imports.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the krónur shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports less imports of goods, converted to krónur at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods. A negative number is a trade deficit.
trade_balance.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the krónur shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending (+) or borrowing (-), % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The gap between what government takes in and what it spends in a year, across all levels of government. A negative number is a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · current account balance, % of GDP, annual.
current_account.description: The balance of trade in goods and services plus income and transfers with the rest of the world. A negative number means the country is borrowing from abroad.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · foreign direct investment, net inflows, % of GDP, annual.
fdi.description: Long-term investment into the country by foreign companies and investors, such as building factories or buying a lasting stake in a business.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per ISK 100 (100 ÷ the published ISK per US$), from 1981.
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars 100 krónur buy. A rising number means a stronger króna.
